59b4660c9819d21d97621fadcac9e93be556164c.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report BRICKSTORM, a Go-based backdoor used in an espionage campaign against US legal, SaaS, BPO and technology organisations since March 2025. The activity is attributed to UNC5221 and closely related, suspected China-nexus clusters. The actor deploys the backdoor on network appliances that lack endpoint detection, targets VMware vCenter, clones sensitive virtual machines, and reads mailboxes through Microsoft Entra ID enterprise applications. Average dwell time was 393 days. The report gives hunting guidance and YARA rules.

hedges: Report says cloud malware delivery trend probably reflects trust in cloud domains and the scale of operations from them.
Report says GC2 gets commands from Google Sheets, likely to obfuscate the malicious activity.
Report says storing malware as encrypted ZIP files is likely in an effort to evade detection.
Report says the DICELOADER campaign appeared to target financial services, based on the phishing emails found.
Report says it cannot comment on the root cause of the 14 compromised customer website incidents.
Report says the misconfigured SQL instances likely had weak passwords or no password at all.
Report says the growth of Go-language tools is likely due to the language's flexibility and ease of adding modules.
Report speculates that state actors may pose as non-state actors to complicate attribution or deflect blame.

5982e26060e1f5716c477568072fbc86f62adcf7.summary: The Register reports, citing the Taipei Times and Liberty Times, that Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau gave 250 USB drives as prizes at a December 2017 security quiz. 54 drives were infected via a supplier's computer with an old data-stealing virus, XtbSeDuA.exe, which targets 32-bit machines. Stolen data was forwarded to a relay server in Poland, which the police say has been shut down. 34 drives are still in circulation. No threat actor is named, and the report says there is no suggestion espionage was a motive.
